summary.headline: Ion Exchange Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell 49% YoY to INR 32 crore (4.54% margin) on 20% revenue growth to INR 701 crore, with treatment solutions still loss-making.
summary.overview: Consolidated operating income rose 20% YoY to INR 701 crore, but EBITDA fell 49% to INR 32 crore and PAT was INR 3 crore (0.44% margin). Management split the former engineering segment into Treatment Solutions, Industrial Products and Lifecycle Services, and reported Specialty Chemicals and Consumer Products separately. Treatment Solutions posted a EBIT loss of INR 17 crore on legacy projects, while Industrial Products margin rose to 11.89%. Management said Roha resin capacity is ramping slower than expected and guidance will be reviewed by end of Q2.

financial_highlights.value: INR 112 crore / loss of INR 34 lakh
financial_highlights.change: +33% revenue YoY; loss was INR 45 lakh
excludes Hyundai win of about USD 52 million

segments.name: Treatment Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 210 crore (+14% YoY) with EBIT loss of INR 17 crore, hit by legacy projects including the UP project. Dispatches to GCC resumed post-quarter; a Hyundai contract of about USD 52 million (over INR 500 crore per Q&A) was won after quarter end.

segments.name: Industrial Products
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 105 crore (+14% YoY) and EBIT INR 13 crore, margin 11.89% vs under 6% a year ago, driven by water treatment solutions and membranes. Institutional products moved here from Consumer.

segments.name: Lifecycle Services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 72 crore (+28% YoY) and EBIT INR 7 crore (9.92% margin vs 10.55%), with margin pressure from higher input costs. Includes a 20-year O&M concession in Oman with PDO.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 230 crore (+21% YoY) but EBIT INR 22 crore (-52% YoY), impacted by geopolitics and Roha ramp-up costs; Roha cost drag about 6% of segment margin. FX gain in the prior-year quarter also reversed (about 3-4 pts).

segments.name: Consumer Products
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 112 crore (+33% YoY) with a small loss of INR 34 lakh vs INR 45 lakh a year ago; breakeven targeted in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Specialty Chemicals capacity to grow at least 50% over the next couple of years as Roha reaches full capacity over about four years, with asset turnover just under 2x.
Roha utilisation guidance of 25% in year one is still held but described as softer than expected; management will review by end of Q2 FY27.
UP legacy project is not expected to close in FY27 and will spill into FY28, dependent on government fund flows; other large legacy project expected to see significant progress by FY27 end.
Consumer Products targeted to break even in FY27.
Management aims to restore double-digit profitability over time; no timeline given. Input costs expected to moderate if crude stays near USD 80.
capex_capacity: Roha resin plant commissioned and in stabilisation; with Ankleshwar debottlenecking, total resin capacity expected to reach about 5x the pre-Roha level (Phase I doubles capacity, Phase II plus debottlenecking takes it to about 5x).
Pharma resin capacity at Ankleshwar (FDA-approved) to expand 6x, targeted within the next 12 months; described as asset-light, technology-led rather than capex-heavy.
Membrane business: second Goa plant under construction to add UF and MBR capacity; tie-up with MANN+HUMMEL for UF PVDF technology. Management targets 3x business growth over the years.
Standard plants capacity expanded across Hosur, Goa and Wada.
Management would not disclose capital earmarked for BOOT/BOO service projects, saying it will remain asset-light.
demand_pricing: Hyundai contract of about USD 52 million (over INR 500 crore) won post quarter end; supplied to an EPC, FOB Mumbai, kickoff under way.
Bid pipeline stood at INR 9,777 crore as of the call.

Price increases taken across customers and segments, but pass-through lags input cost increases; management sees some moderation in input costs with crude near USD 80 vs over USD 100 in March-April 2026.
Geopolitical situation (West Asia) impacted invoicing and dispatches; Roha volumes expected to lean on overseas markets, including North America after WQA certification.
UP project unexecuted portion is about 11% of June order backlog; receivable exposure said to be broadly unchanged over recent quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Portugal/Iberian acquisition: progress and margin profile versus India?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisition was about three years ago and integration is complete; management declined to give geography-specific margins but said margins would be similar to or better than India, with four of five segments present there (not Consumer).

qa_highlights.question: Why reclassify segments and is a corporate action or separate listing planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Engineering was not showing the full picture of products, services and solutions; no separate listing or corporate action is planned, and about 60% of the company is now products, chemicals and services versus about 40% treatment solutions.

qa_highlights.question: Roha 5x capacity claim and link to resin revenue of about INR 500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: 5x is a group-level resin capacity figure across Roha and Ankleshwar after debottlenecking; Phase I doubles capacity, and Phase II plus debottlenecking takes output to about 5x the original Ankleshwar capacity. Management aspires to about 10% of global resin volume and gave no segment split.

qa_highlights.question: Pharma resin 6x expansion: timeline, capex and revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion is in process and targeted within 12 months; management said capex is manageable and the constraint is technical know-how, with asset turn well above Roha's 2-2.5x. FY26 pharma revenue was not disclosed and the segment stays within Specialty Chemicals.

qa_highlights.question: Treatment Solutions profitability: why has EBIT fallen over five years and what is the path back?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to large legacy projects, now in final stages but with a sizable portion remaining, plus a move to selective bidding, advanced and emerging solutions, and walking away from difficult projects. Cost overruns on the large project were acknowledged as a meaningful impact.

qa_highlights.question: Did the WQA certification contribute to Q1 revenue, and what is the North America outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: No quantification was given for Q1 contribution; management said a significant, though not majority, part of Roha volume is expected to go to overseas markets, notably North America, after WQA certification.

qa_highlights.question: Roha 25% first-year utilisation guidance and Consumer breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Roha guidance of 25% is still held but has been softer than expected; management will update by end of Q2 FY27. Consumer Products breakeven is the first FY27 target, with single-digit margins to be discussed later.

qa_highlights.question: Specialty Chemicals margin compression: Roha drag and other factors?
qa_highlights.answer: Roha impact on segment margin was about 6%; the prior-year FX gain reversal was about 3-4 points; and pass-through of input cost increases lagged, with some moderation expected if crude stays near USD 80.

qa_highlights.question: UP legacy project: unexecuted portion, receivables and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Unexecuted UP portion is about 11% of the June order backlog of INR 2,473 crore; receivable exposure is materially unchanged over recent quarters. Closure is not expected in FY27 and will depend on government fund flows, which have started to come in.

risks_watch: Treatment Solutions EBIT loss of INR 17 crore; recovery depends on the UP project (government-funded, about 11% of June backlog unexecuted) and at least one other large legacy project, with cost overruns acknowledged.
Roha resin plant utilisation: 25% first-year guidance is softer than expected and will be re-examined by end of Q2 FY27; the Roha cost drag was about 6% of Specialty Chemicals segment margin.
Input cost pass-through lag and crude-linked raw materials (amines, monomers); management sees moderation only if crude stays near USD 80 after levels above USD 100 in March-April 2026.
Geopolitical disruption (West Asia) affecting invoicing and dispatches to GCC; Hyundai USD 52 million order (supplied via an EPC, FOB Mumbai) could be at risk if the crisis persists.
Capital intensity of BOOT/BOO and O&M concessions, such as the 20-year Oman PDO contract; management would not disclose capital earmarked.

Consumer Products breakeven target in FY27 and Lifecycle Services margin (9.92% vs 10.55%) to monitor next quarter; the company will also provide reconciliation data to bridge reclassified segment numbers.
key_quotes: I agree that the performance in the first quarter has been disappointing, and it is a combination, as you said, some of the legacy projects which continue to grind through.
So, we don't want to give a feeling that we are out of the woods. We are not.
Having said that, we do not want to increase our exposure as a company to more receivables unless and until the funds flow happen.
So, we expect a substantial increase of at least 50% in this capacity over the next couple of years.
summary.management_tone: Candid about weakness: the CEO called the Q1 performance "disappointing" and said the legacy projects are not "out of the woods", while stressing a "clear path" back to double-digit profitability without a timeline. Management was evasive on quantification (WQA revenue contribution, pharma resin revenue, segment-level Roha economics, UP timing), and reiterated that the UP project depends on government fund flows.

adds.what: Roha resin plant (commissioned, in stabilisation); with Ankleshwar debottlenecking, total resin capacity to about 5x pre-Roha level
Pharma resin capacity at Ankleshwar (FDA-approved) to expand 6x, asset-light
Second Goa membrane plant adding UF and MBR capacity
Specialty Chemicals capacity increase of at least 50% over next couple of years

growth.why: Consolidated revenue grew 20% YoY to INR 701 crore and an INR 2,473 crore order book plus a ~USD 52m Hyundai win support near-term growth, but Roha ramp is slower than expected, the Roha utilisation guide is under review by end Q2, and EBITDA fell 49%, so the outlook is mixed.
